title: Dynamic priority, latency-aware event buffer for console metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Console telemetry ingest sees bursty tenant traffic that forces a trade-off between batching efficiency and tail latency. Current single FIFO buffers cause either large latency spikes for high-priority events or poor GPU utilization downstream. Goal: implement a memory- and time-bounded, priority-aware buffering layer in the ingest pipeline that preserves tenant fairness, supports latency SLOs for critical events, and exposes admission/backpressure signals to upstream gateways.

Scope: design and implement a windowed priority queue that groups events into small batch windows, prioritizes SLO-tagged events (e.g., control-plane, billing alerts), and dynamically adjusts admission thresholds per-tenant based on token-bucket rate and recent service-time telemetry. The buffer will emit both regular batches and emergency flushes for high-priority items, integrate with our checkpointing for exactly-once delivery semantics, and instrument new telemetry for observability and auto-scaling tuning.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Kickoff: design spike completed; prototype in go-runner branch. Spike showed 2.3x throughput for mixed workloads and 40ms median additional latency for regular events when emergency flush is rare.
2026-03-01 - Review feedback from PM (Lina Moreno): request to add per-tenant fairness SLA and a kill-switch to disable priority promotion for tenants in abuse state. Added to tasks.

2026-03-02 - Engineering review (PR #8123): initial implementation of windowed buffer. Code review by Rahul Gupta: ask to add more unit tests around watermark edge cases and to document eviction behavior.

2026-03-03 - Observability sync: agreed to emit metrics: buffer_queue_depth{priority}, window_flush_latency_p50/p95, evicted_events_count, admission_rejects_by_tenant. Dashboard template created: Console > Ingest > PriorityBuffer (draft).
decisions: Use multi-level in-memory priority buckets with time-window batching instead of a single sorted priority queue to reduce O(log n) tail cost and GC churn.
Adopt a hybrid flush policy: time-window expiry (default 20ms) OR size threshold (e.g., 128 events) OR emergency flush for priority level >= 90.
Store durable checkpoint state for each window in Kafka offsets + compacted watermark keys in RocksDB to support exactly-once on retries.
Expose a backpressure/graceful-degradation header to the gateway (x-ingest-pressure: low|medium|high) based on buffer fullness and eviction rate.
Tenant fairness: implement leaky-bucket admission with soft-quotas; when over-utilized, throttle non-SLA tenants first and surface rejected samples for analysis.
Do not attempt to co-locate KV cache with this buffer; keep in separate process to allow independent scaling.
Security: no PII will be persisted in the buffer; all events must follow existing redaction rules before enqueuing.
tasks: Implement in-memory multi-bucket buffer with configurable windows and priority thresholds (ENG owner: Jonas Kim).
Integrate window checkpointing with stream consumer offsets and durable metadata (use existing checkpoint interface from ENG-30458).
Add admission control module (token-bucket per-tenant) and an API to set tenant soft-quotas via Console config.
Wire up backpressure header emission and test end-to-end with ingress gateway simulator (load-test harness).
Create unit and integration tests for watermark edge cases, eviction cases, and recovery after process restart.
Add telemetry and dashboard tile: queue depth by priority, flush latency p50/p95/p999, evictions, admission rejects, and per-tenant throttle signals.
Run 48-hour canary with 5% of traffic from staging, validate no regression on p99 for critical control-plane events.
Docs: update runbook with mitigation steps and knob descriptions; add config guide in Confluence.
Security review input: confirm redaction hooks are invoked pre-enqueue and document audit check (owner: Security Ops).
acceptance_criteria: High-priority events (marked SLA) maintain p99 < 200ms through the buffer under 95th percentile traffic bursts observed in prod traces.
Buffer reduces tail batching cost (tokens/second) by at least 15% vs current baseline without increasing median latency for non-SLA events by more than 50ms.
No loss of events in canary; checkpoint/replay test passes and consumed offsets align with durable metadata after a simulated crash/restart.
Dashboard surfaces buffer metrics and alert: buffer_queue_depth > 80% for > 30s and evicted_events_count > 0 triggers a P1 incident policy.
Feature has a feature-flagged rollout path and a manual kill-switch; rollout plan documented in the ticket.
